## Goal and research tracks

Add a small explicit typed whitelist for equality/inequality, ordered comparisons and checked arithmetic. Inputs must have relational bindings before evaluation, arithmetic must not generate an unbounded recursive carrier domain, and invalid/unsafe programs must not return a partial relation. Representative age, range and time filters must agree across independent oracles and supported execution paths. Dates/references/null and arbitrary functions are not implied.

Four parallel native Sol 6.1 max tracks cover semantics/termination, pinned DuckDB SQL/error behavior and performance, cross-language numeric/reference semantics, and admission/resource/transaction boundaries. Each track uses fresh primary sources and isolated probes; original, frozen and accepted implementation sources are read-only during this gate.

## Findings that constrain implementation

- **Finite domain is a design constraint, not a work-limit claim.** Safe positive Datalog has finitely many possible tuples over its finite active domain; expression results must remain ephemeral filter temporaries rather than head values or new interned recursive IDs. Body-only filters preserve that argument. This application is our design inference from the [formal fixed-point/size analysis](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/01oasics/oasics-vol138-rw2024%2Brw2025/html/OASIcs.RW.2024-2025.7/OASIcs.RW.2024-2025.7.html). [Soufflé's arithmetic documentation](https://souffle-lang.github.io/arguments) deliberately permits broader value generation, so its surface should not be copied indiscriminately.
- **A bound variable is not yet a complete join witness.** Throwing a checked fault on a partial binding can invent an error when a later relation is empty. Conversely, pruning on an earlier false filter or pre-existing head tuple can hide an error. The leading design evaluates filters on complete relational candidates before head deduplication; false does not suppress other checked faults. Rule unfolding, demand pruning and filter pushdown require additional error-observation proofs.
- **SQL Boolean syntax is not the language contract.** Fresh pinned DuckDB source/probes distinguish eager projected conjunctions from shrinking-selection WHERE evaluation, and optimizer-on/off probes differ. A separate totalized status/value SQL oracle is being checked rather than inheriting implicit casts or short circuit. This also aligns with the general caution in [PostgreSQL's expression-evaluation documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-expressions.html#SYNTAX-EXPRESS-EVAL), not a claim that the two engines implement identical optimizers.
- **Output ordering and filter compatibility are different.** Existing cross-tag sort order is only canonical output ordering. The candidate equality semantics are total tagged identity (unlike tags false, inequality true), with strict same-tag ordering/arithmetic and no coercion. Ordinary relational unification remains a nonmatch for unlike tags.
- **Nondefault native floating-point state is a newly diagnosed gap.** Isolated x86-64 probes show changed rounding, FTZ/DAZ and permitted FMA contraction can violate per-node browser binary64 parity. DAZ can even alter item-1 public Value subnormal admission before arithmetic. Normal-state accepted tests are not a proof for these altered states. Focused primary-source research selects bitwise finite admission/zero/equality/order/interning plus fail-closed typed entry guards, strict compiler controls and bit-exact adverse-state tests. It does not alter DuckDB's host FP controls. A bounded correctly-rounded BigInt decimal parser also closes the documented long-decimal JS conversion portability gap without narrowing existing literals.
- **Bound the parser independently of text size.** Separate structural/node/depth limits and at/beyond tests are required; [SQLite's official limits rationale](https://sqlite.org/limits.html) illustrates why a bounded input string is not itself a recursive-stack proof. Existing legacy work counters should remain unchanged for old programs, with additive expression/string-byte charges explicitly defined.
- **Atomicity has a boundary.** One native result and one store command are materialized before return; this does not certify arbitrary multi-invocation SQL streaming or unrelated side effects. The existing post-COMMIT physical-size exception also carries a committed position and must not be mislabeled rollback.

## Selected contract and gate before code

Read [the selected contract](CONTRACT.md), [semantic proof and alternatives](semantics/RESEARCH.md), [pinned SQL/performance research](sql/REPORT.md), [cross-language numeric/FP research](browser/REPORT.md) and [admission/atomicity research](admission/REPORT.md). Their source ledgers and raw probe evidence accompany the snapshot. The shared contract governs any labeled older proposal in an individual report. Preserve the completed research and exact syntax/numeric/error/seed/resource decisions, then authorize disjoint implementation ownership with independent acceptance fixtures. In particular, constant arithmetic faults behind empty joins must not be accidentally raised by eager folding, and ground filter-only rules must evaluate their one empty-binding candidate rather than seed unconditionally.

No production readiness, item-2 completion, deployment, merge, force push, GitHub deletion, Codex task or user-computer action is claimed.
